Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Bangladesh's reply. As Tamim Iqbal and Saif Hassan start their innings and Shaheen Afridi to start with the ball.

On the other hand, Bangladesh bowlers toiled hard and were superb this morning. All the pacers of Bangladesh were into the wickets. As Abu Jayed, Rubel Hossain and Ebadot Hossain bowled their heart out. Taijul Islam did well to contain the runs and built pressure at one end thus helping the pacers to reap rewards. Jayed and Rubel both ended with a 3-wicket haul and Taijul and Ebadot both getting 2 and 1 wickets respectively.

Pakistan would be happy here that they have managed a lead of over 200 runs. For putting Pakistan in this position, the applause should go to Shan Masood who upfront played a responsible innings and was involved in partnerships with skipper Azhar Ali and then with Babar Azam. Though he departed soon after his ton but then Asad Shafiq and Babar Azam joined forces and stitched a 137-run stand. But since their dismissal, it was a downward slide for the hosts. If not for Haris Sohail's 75, they would have ended on a much lower score.

Hossain then bowled a delivery that came back in to dismiss Asad Shafiq. Since then the Pakistan innings seems to have fallen apart as Mohammad Rizwan failed to occupy the crease by playing an unnecessary shot. Despite losing 4 wickets in the session, Pakistan are in a strong position as they lead by 187 runs and have Haris Sohail their last recognized batsman out in the middle. He has also reached his fifty and would look for the support of the tail to extend Pakistan's domination. Whereas, Bangladesh would look to wipe out the tail as quickly as possible. Shan Masood and Babar Azam were the stars on Day 2 as they both notched up their tons. Asad Shafiq will also look to get to his Test ton. Babar Azam is still out there and Pakistan would hope that he guides Pakistan to a massive first innings lead. Bangladesh were poor with their bowling effort and were seen short of ideas as the Pakistan batsmen kept on milking the runs. Only two of their bowlers out of the five they used could get into the wickets column. They would hope to improve on that. Hello and welcome to Day 3. Who will have the say today? Will Pakistan continue their merry way or will Bangladesh stage a comeback?

If Bangladesh are to make a comeback in this Test then there is only one way and that is they need to pick wickets early on Day 3 and in a heap or else they could find themselves going on a leather hunt. Day 3 is also known as the moving day in a Test match. That will decide who has the advantage. Do join us for the coverage of Day 3 at 1000 local (0500 GMT). Till then cheers and take care!

Barring the first hour of the day, Bangladesh's bowling was toothless and was seen wanting for ideas. They tried everything they could but failed to strike at regular intervals. Talking about their bowlers Abu Jayed and Taijul Islam worked the most in the field. The latter though bowled the maximum. He though returned with just a lone wicket of the centurion Shan Masood. The other bowler to enter the wickets column was Abu Jayed who scalped a couple of wickets. All in all a tiring long day in the field for the visitors.

Earlier in the day, Pakistan started their reply for Bangladesh's 233 but failed to get a dream start as Abu Jayed struck in his very first to remove Abid Ali for a duck. Then came the stand between Shan Masood and Azhar Ali which revived Pakistan's innings. Just when it looked that Pakistan are cruising, Azhar Ali lost his wicket at the stroke of Lunch. But that did not affect the home team as it continued to score runs. Masood soon departed after his 3rd Test ton but Babar continued his good work after being let off the hook early on in his innings. Babar reached his 5th Test ton and him along with Asad Shafiq ensured that there is no further casualty and the duo batted out to see off the day.

A brilliant session from Pakistan's point of view. They managed to score 136 runs in 32.5 overs without losing a wicket. It all started with Babar Azam continuing from where he left before the Tea interval. Soon Asad Shafiq too joined the party as the duo started to milk runs at will. In the process, Babar reached his 5th Test ton and Shafiq too reached his 27th Test half-ton. They both added 137 runs for the 4th wicket and strengthened Pakistan's position and grip on the match as from trail they went into the lead. Currently, Pakistan lead by 109 and have 7 wickets in hand. On the other hand, Bangladesh bowlers were clueless and their attack looked toothless too. They tried everything from short stuff to full deliveries but nothing worked for them. In the end, with tiring bowlers, they just hoped for the batsmen to commit some errors but they never came.

We are back for the final session of Day 2. Also known as the happening session in a Test match. Pakistan batsmen Babar Azam and Asad Shafiq walk out to resume their innings. Bangladesh players are out too. Taijul Islam will start the proceedings for the final session of Day 2.

The session started with Pakistan coming out all guns blazing. They counter-attacked the Bangladesh bowlers and clobbered them all around the park. With Babar at the crease and Shafiq for his company, Bangladesh would look to capitalise on this opening. Join us for the final session at 1500 local (1000 GMT).

We are back for the second session. The Bangladesh players are out in the middle. Shan Masood and Babar Azam will resume their innings for the hosts. Babar Azam is yet to open his account and he has already faced 14 balls. Taijul Islam will start the proceedings for the second session.

Talking of Pakistan's batting, it did not start on the right note for the hosts as they lost their new batting sensation Abid Ali for a duck. But skipper, Azhar Ali and opener Shan Masood steadied the ship with a 91-run stand. Masood also reached his 7th Test fifty in the process. Just when it looked that Pakistan were starting to take the upper hand in the game, Abu Jayed struck for the second time to send the Pakistan skipper back into the hut. Trailing by 138 runs with Babar Azam and Shan Masood still out there it should be easy for the hosts to wipe out the deficit. Will Bangladesh continue their good work from the first session? Or Will Pakistan come back strongly?  Do join us for the afternoon session at 1240 local (0740 GMT).

A good session for Bangladesh as they managed to send Abid Ali in the first over of the Pakistan innings, who was on fire after making his debut against Sri Lanka earlier in January. They kept it tight and did not allow the Pakistan batters to overpower them. The pacers initially used the conditions to good effect as they tested the batsmen with everything they had in their armoury.
So, an engrossing session of Test cricket witnessed between Pakistan and Bangladesh. 95 runs were scored in this session but two important wickets were lost by Pakistan in the process.
